provenance.instrument: West Caln Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 350 Zoning, Ord. No. 2026-01 of 6-17-2026), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 WE4254, Township of West Caln, Chester County (350-200E: 'The word "Township" shall mean West Caln Township, Chester County, Pennsylvania'). Ord. No. 2026-01 replaced the 2006 zoning chapter. District use lists and lot, yard and height figures are text in Articles IV to IX. The attachments are a road map, model timber harvesting rules, a plant list and the zoning map. Floodplain, steep slope and riparian buffer rules are in Article X of the zoning chapter. New Laws: none
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 06-17-2026.' New Laws: none
checks: Supplemental dwelling unit: 'a smaller secondary dwelling unit within an existing single-family detached dwelling or within a new or existing accessory building on the same lot as the principal single-family detached dwelling' (350-1101C(13)). By right in AP (350-401A(13)), a special exception in V (350-701A(2)(g), 350-701B(2)(g)), a conditional use in SRR, RR and RC (350-501C(5), 350-601C(4), 350-801C(1)). MP lists no house and no supplemental dwelling unit by name. It permits 'Agricultural accessory use, as per 350-1101B' by right with nothing left out (350-901A(2)), and 350-1101B(6) lists 'Residential accessory uses, as per 350-1101C', which include the supplemental dwelling unit. So on a farm lot in MP a unit may be by right, and the additional farm-related dwellings of 350-1101B(9) are by right there too

Standards: it stays accessory and secondary to the house. The district's area and bulk regulations apply to the lot. One per lot, two on a lot over 10 acres. Either the house or the unit must be occupied by the owner. At most 25% of the house's total floor area and at least 400 sq ft. Two off-street spaces beyond the house's own (350-1101C(13)(a) to (h)). Floor area leaves out garages, attics without floors, porches and cellars (350-201 'Floor area')

Where it may go: inside the existing house, which may include an attached garage or upper story, keeping the look of a single-family house, with entrances on the rear or side, or in a new or existing accessory building on the lot. Additions must meet the district's area and bulk rules (350-1101C(13)(e))

Accessory buildings: rear or side yard only, no further forward than the front line of the house except garages, at least 10 ft from lot lines and 15 ft for a building over 200 sq ft, and at most 15 ft tall unless the chapter says otherwise (350-1101A(2) to (4)). Agricultural accessory uses instead follow the district height (350-1101B). On a corner lot accessory buildings stay behind the setback lines of both streets (350-1201D)

Agricultural accessory dwelling unit and other additional farm-related dwellings: a conditional use in AP and by right in MP, for family members or farm workers of the farm, one on a parent agricultural tract of 10 to 25 acres and up to two on a larger tract, at least 25 ft from all lot lines. An agricultural accessory dwelling unit expands an existing house, may use an attached garage or upper story, may add up to 100% of the house's gross floor area or 2,000 sq ft, whichever is less, and needs an owner-occupant. A conversion of an existing structure on the farm, such as a barn, may hold one farm-related unit under 350-1132. In AP each counts toward the parent tract's lot and unit limit (350-1101B(9), 350-401C(2), 350-901A(2), 350-402C(1))

Residential conversion of a single-family detached dwelling into two or three units: a conditional use in AP and a special exception in V. It must keep the look of a single house with one front entrance, have no major structural change, meet the single-family lot and bulk figures, and give each unit at least 450 sq ft (efficiency), 550 (one bedroom), 700 (two) or 800 (three, the most) (350-401C(6), 350-701A(2)(b), 350-1132)

Historic resources: a structure on the West Caln Township Historic Resources Survey may be converted into a single-family detached dwelling, a twin or a townhouse, or under 350-1132, by conditional use, as an additional principal use on a lot that already has one 'without requiring additional variance relief' (350-2007). The Board may also modify lot, density, coverage, yard, height and parking figures for it (350-2008). New construction on a property with a historic resource needs Historical Commission review before a permit (350-2005A)
V and RC permit a twin and a two-family detached dwelling (duplex, two units one over the other) by right as new buildings (350-701A(1), 350-801A(2), (3))

Parking: off-street demand follows ITE Parking Generation, and 'a fraction of 1/2 or more shall be rounded up, and a fraction of less than 1/2 rounded down' (350-1303A, D). Parking may take up no more than half of a required front yard (350-1302D)

Floodplain (Article X): within the Identified Floodplain Area 'any new construction or substantial improvements shall be prohibited' except listed uses, and modifications to existing structures and adaptive reuse of an existing building are special exceptions (350-1002A(4)(a)[4][b], (4)(b)). An accessory structure there 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' and may have at most 200 sq ft of floor area (350-1002A(4)(b)[5]). 'No variances shall be granted for a proposed accessory structure that exceeds 600 square feet in size', and any variance for one needs a signed nonconversion agreement (350-1002A(7)(b)[1][c]). In an AE area without a floodway no new construction within 50 ft landward of the top of bank unless DEP issues a permit (350-1002A(3)(b)[2][b][ii]). Manufactured homes are prohibited within 50 ft landward of the top of bank (350-1002A(4)(f)[2]). Fill is prohibited unless a variance is granted

Riparian forest buffer: Zone One runs at least 35 ft from the top of the stream bank and allows no vegetation or land disturbance beyond listed activities. Zone Two adds 65 ft, of which at most 20% may be disturbed. The buffer may never be cut below 75 ft (350-201 'Riparian forest buffer', 350-1002C)

Steep slopes: at most 30% of moderately steep slopes (15% to 25%) and 15% of very steep slopes (25% or more) may be disturbed, and on very steep slopes only for timber harvesting, the minimum grading for a road or driveway to the principal use, or utility lines (350-1002B). So a building may not stand on very steep slopes

Density: RR allows 0.5 dwelling units per acre of net tract area under the conventional option and 0.75 under the cluster option, and RC 4, 1.25 or 1 by services. These count the units a development may hold on its tract at subdivision. They are not a cap a later unit on one lot must meet (350-602, 350-802B). AP limits the lots or dwelling units subdivided from a parent tract (one for 10 to 14.99 acres up to seven at 150 acres). It names units under 350-1101B(9) and split-offs as counting, not a supplemental dwelling unit, which is not subdivided from the tract (350-402C(1))

Variances: the Zoning Hearing Board on the hardship findings of 350-1707. No bar on a use variance was found. A lot nonconforming only in area may be built on if the yards are met, otherwise a special exception (350-1504A). 'An existing structure located on a lot nonconforming as to area may be used for the use permitted in the district in which it is located, provided the structure complies with all bulk requirements of that district' (350-1504C)

Resource disturbance caps, which apply with any zoning or building permit, conditional use, special exception or variance: floodplain 0%, wetlands 0% and Zone One riparian buffer 0%, Zone Two 20%, moderately steep slopes 30%, very steep slopes 15%, critical woodlands 5% and non-critical woodlands 35% for residential uses. They 'may be modified where federal or state permits have been obtained' (350-1003A(1)(c)). Wetlands may not be built upon or disturbed except under state or federal permits, and at most 20% of a wetland margin may be disturbed (350-1002E)

Front yards in any district may be reduced to the average setback of existing buildings within 100 ft on each side of the new building on the same block, never into the street right-of-way (350-1201B). V has its own averaging rule, between 10 ft and 30 ft (350-702A(4))

In V and RC 'Garages accessed from the street frontage shall be setback a minimum of 20 feet from the front facade of the dwelling' (350-703E, 350-803G). Flag lots are not permitted in V, RC or MP (350-703J, 350-803I, 350-903A)

MP figures for all uses: one acre, 150 ft wide at the building line and 125 ft at the street, front 50 ft, side 30 ft, rear 50 ft, each 75 ft when abutting or across from nonindustrial uses or districts, building coverage 45%, lot coverage 55%, 45 ft (350-902A). Any other use of a similar character to those permitted in MP is a conditional use (350-901C(35))

Short-term rental: a short-term rental accessory to an owner-occupied single-family house is subject to the same design configurations as a supplemental dwelling unit, and is licensed under Chapter 262 (Property Registration) (350-1101C(14)). It is lodging, not a home. A temporary structure permit may include temporary residential uses for six months, and recreational vehicles may not be used as living quarters (350-1101F(2), C(9), 350-1204B(1))
provenance.notes: Zoning office: West Caln Township Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-17. Open points: the unit on a farm lot in SRR and RR (by right as an agricultural accessory use under 350-501A(6), 350-601A(7) and 350-1101B(6), or a conditional use under 350-501C(5), 350-601C(4)), the height of a unit in an accessory building on a farm (district height under the 350-1101B lead, or 15 ft under 350-1101A(4)), and whether a lot below the district minimum may hold a unit (350-1504).

A separate 'agricultural accessory dwelling unit' is a farm-related dwelling in AP (350-1101B(9))

value.name: Agricultural accessory dwelling unit or other additional farm-related dwelling (AP)
value.conditions: Only for family members or farm workers of the farm on the parent agricultural tract. One on a parent tract of 10 to 25 acres, up to two on a larger tract, and each counts toward the tract's lot and unit limit. An agricultural accessory dwelling unit expands an existing single-family house, may use an attached garage or upper story, keeps the look of one house, may add up to 100% of the house's gross floor area or 2,000 sq ft, whichever is less, and needs an owner-occupant of the house or the unit. Other options are one unit in a converted farm structure, such as a barn, under 350-1132 or another house under Article IV. Additional dwellings are set back at least 25 ft from all lot lines

requires.condition: A parent agricultural tract of at least 10 acres
The lot is in agricultural use and the unit is for family members or farm workers of that use

value.note: The code calls it an agricultural accessory dwelling unit. In AP a supplemental dwelling unit is by right, so this listing matters only for a farm unit that does not meet the supplemental unit's standards

value.name: Supplemental dwelling unit on a farm, as an agricultural accessory use (MP)
value.conditions: MP permits 'Agricultural accessory use, as per 350-1101B' by right, with nothing left out. 350-1101B(6) lists 'Residential accessory uses, as per 350-1101C', and those include the supplemental dwelling unit of 350-1101C(13). The supplemental dwelling unit's own standards apply: inside the house with entrances on the rear or side, or in a new or existing accessory building, at most 25% of the house's floor area and at least 400 sq ft, one unit (two on a lot over 10 acres), an owner living in the house or the unit, and two parking spaces beyond the house's own. An accessory building for agricultural accessory uses follows the district height ('Maximum height shall follow height regulations for the district', 350-1101B). Whether that or the 15 ft of 350-1101A(4) binds a unit in an accessory building is not settled. MP's own figures are one acre, front 50 ft, side 30 ft and rear 50 ft (75 ft each when abutting or across from nonindustrial uses or districts), building coverage 45% and a height of 45 ft

requires.condition: The lot is in agricultural use (or holds a CAO, CAFO or mushroom production facility), with the farm owner's or operator's single-family house, and the unit is incidental and subordinate to that use

value.note: MP has no single-family house of its own. The farm owner's or operator's dwelling is the house the unit goes with. Off a farm, MP has no path for a unit other than a use similar to those permitted, by conditional use (350-901C(35))

value.name: Agricultural accessory dwelling unit or other additional farm-related dwelling (MP)
value.conditions: MP permits all agricultural accessory uses of 350-1101B by right, including the additional farm-related dwellings of 350-1101B(9). Only for family members or farm workers of the farm. One on a parent tract of 10 to 25 acres, up to two on a larger tract, at least 25 ft from all lot lines. An agricultural accessory dwelling unit expands an existing house, may use an attached garage or upper story, may add up to 100% of the house's gross floor area or 2,000 sq ft, whichever is less, and needs an owner-occupant. Other options are one unit in a converted farm structure under 350-1132 or another dwelling

requires.condition: A parent agricultural tract of at least 10 acres
The lot is in agricultural use and the unit is for family members or farm workers of that use

value.note: The code calls it an agricultural accessory dwelling unit. It is a conditional use in AP and by right in MP

value.name: Supplemental dwelling unit on a farm, as an agricultural accessory use (SRR, RR)
value.conditions: SRR and RR permit 'Agricultural accessory use as per 350-1101B, with the exception of 350-1101B(9)' by right, and 350-1101B(6) lists 'Residential accessory uses, as per 350-1101C' without leaving out the supplemental dwelling unit. The supplemental dwelling unit's own standards apply: inside the house with entrances on the rear or side, or in a new or existing accessory building, at most 25% of the house's floor area and at least 400 sq ft, one unit (two on a lot over 10 acres), an owner living in the house or the unit, and two parking spaces beyond the house's own. An accessory building for agricultural accessory uses follows the district height ('Maximum height shall follow height regulations for the district', 350-1101B). Whether that or the 15 ft of 350-1101A(4) binds a unit in an accessory building is not settled

requires.condition: The lot is in agricultural use (or holds a CAO, CAFO or mushroom production facility), with the farm owner's or operator's single-family house, and the unit is incidental and subordinate to that use

disputed_path.note: The district lists name the supplemental dwelling unit as a conditional use, and their by-right residential accessory uses leave it out in words. Off a farm the conditional use is the only path

value.note: A reading of the code on a farm lot, not settled. Ask the zoning officer which path applies

value.name: Residential conversion into two or three units (AP)
value.conditions: A single-family detached dwelling divided into a two or three family dwelling. It keeps the look of one house with one front entrance, other entrances on the side or rear, no major structural change, the single-family lot and bulk figures, separate kitchens and baths, and at least 450 sq ft for an efficiency, 550 for one bedroom, 700 for two and 800 for three (the most). Parking per Article XIII
value.note: A house divided into units, not a unit added to it

value.name: Residential conversion (V)
value.conditions: A single-family detached dwelling divided into two or more units. It keeps the look of one house with one front entrance, other entrances on the side or rear, no major structural change, the single-family lot and bulk figures, separate kitchens and baths, and at least 450 sq ft for an efficiency, 550 for one bedroom, 700 for two and 800 for three (the most). Parking per Article XIII
value.note: A house divided into units, not a unit added to it

value.name: Twin or two-family detached dwelling (V, RC)
value.conditions: A single-family semidetached dwelling (twin) or a two-family detached dwelling (duplex, two units separated by a horizontal party wall). In V the lot is 20,000 sq ft to one acre. In RC the lot and density follow the services: 10,000 sq ft and 4 units per net acre with public or community water and sewer, 25,000 sq ft and 1.25 units per acre with one of them, 30,000 sq ft and 1 unit per acre with neither
value.note: A new two-unit building, not a unit added to an existing house. RC's figure is for a lot with public water and sewer

value.name: Adaptive reuse of a historic resource as a dwelling
value.conditions: A structure on the West Caln Township Historic Resources Survey, such as an old barn or outbuilding, may be converted into a single-family detached dwelling, a twin or a townhouse, or under 350-1132, by conditional use. Where the property already has a principal permitted use, the reuse 'may be permitted as an additional principal use by conditional use and without requiring additional variance relief'. The Board may modify lot area, density, coverage, yard, setback, height and parking figures. Changes must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards and Historical Commission review

requires.condition: The structure is a historic resource on the West Caln Township Historic Resources Survey

value.note: A second dwelling in an existing historic outbuilding on a house lot, which is an ADU in all but name. The code makes it a second principal use, not an accessory unit, and none of the supplemental dwelling unit's caps apply

unlisted_use_path.note: In MP 'Any other use of a similar character of those permitted in this district' is a conditional use before the Board of Supervisors

unlisted_use_scope.quote: Any other use of a similar character of those permitted in this district.

building_types.note: 'within single-family detached dwellings or within a new or existing accessory building on the same lot as the principal single-family detached dwelling'

historic_bypass.note: No historic path for a supplemental dwelling unit. A historic resource may become an additional dwelling by conditional use (see the other paths)

value.condition: A unit inside the house keeps the look of a single-family detached dwelling, and 'Entrances to the supplemental dwelling unit shall be located to the rear or side of the building.' Additions must meet the district's area and bulk requirements.

'The area and bulk regulations of the zoning district shall apply to the lot on which the supplemental dwelling unit is located.' A lot in an RR cluster development takes the cluster figures. An existing lot below the district minimum may still hold a unit inside an existing house, since an existing structure on such a lot 'may be used for the use permitted in the district' if it meets the bulk rules, and a new building needs the yards met or a special exception. Ask the zoning officer to confirm.

Cluster residential development option in RR, with public sewer and water: lots of 20,000 sq ft, 60 ft wide, front 25 ft, side yards 25 ft together and 10 ft on one side, rear 25 ft, building coverage 25%, impervious cover 40%, 35 ft.

AP limits the lots or dwelling units subdivided from a parent tract of record (one for 10 to 14.99 acres, two to 34.99, three to 59.99, four to 89.99, five to 119.99, six to 149.99, and seven at 150 acres plus one per 30 acres more). It names units under 350-1101B(9) and split-offs as counting. A supplemental dwelling unit is not subdivided from the tract, so it reads as not counting. Ask the zoning officer to confirm.

Residential dwellings must stand at least 100 ft from any adjacent agricultural use, CAO, CAFO or mushroom facility in AP, and in SRR and RR at least 100 ft from a CAO, CAFO or mushroom facility and 50 ft from adjacent agricultural uses.

Within the Identified Floodplain Area 'any new construction or substantial improvements shall be prohibited' except the listed uses, and an accessory structure there 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' and may have at most 200 sq ft of floor area. 'No variances shall be granted for a proposed accessory structure that exceeds 600 square feet in size', and a variance for a smaller one needs a signed nonconversion agreement, so a variance does not open a unit in an accessory building there.

no_variance.quote: No variances shall be granted for a proposed accessory structure that exceeds 600 square feet in size
no_variance.note: A variance for a smaller one needs a signed nonconversion agreement, so a variance does not open a unit in an accessory building there

value.condition: In the Identified Floodplain Area 'Modifications to structures existing as of the date of adoption of this chapter' are a special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board. No expansion may raise flood levels in a floodway or more than one foot in an AE area without a floodway, and work costing 50% or more of the building's market value must fully comply, with the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation.

In an AE area without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection Regional Office'.

Zone One of the riparian forest buffer runs at least 35 ft from the top of the stream bank of any watercourse, farther where very steep slopes lie within it, and 'no vegetation disturbance or other land disturbance shall be permitted' there beyond listed activities such as trails and permitted crossings.

Zone Two of the riparian forest buffer adds 65 ft beyond Zone One, and no more than 20% of it may be regraded, built upon or otherwise disturbed. The buffer may never be reduced below 75 ft from the top of the stream bank.

No more than 30% of moderately steep slopes (15% to 25%) and 15% of very steep slopes (25% or more) may be disturbed, and on very steep slopes only for timber, a needed road or driveway, or utilities.

On a property with a structure on the West Caln Township Historic Resources Survey, new additions and new construction need Historical Commission review against the Secretary of the Interior's Standards before a permit is issued.
On very steep slopes (25% or more) disturbance is limited to timber harvesting, the minimum grading for a road or driveway to the principal use, and utility lines. A building may not stand there.

Disturbance caps apply with any permit or approval: floodplain, wetlands and Zone One of the riparian buffer 0%, Zone Two 20%, moderately steep slopes 30%, very steep slopes 15%, critical woodlands 5% and non-critical woodlands 35% for residential uses. They may be modified where federal or state permits have been obtained. Wetlands may not be built upon except under state or federal permits.
The front yard may be reduced to the average setback of existing buildings within 100 ft on each side of the new building on the same block, never into the street right-of-way.
'Garages accessed from the street frontage shall be setback a minimum of 20 feet from the front facade of the dwelling.'

The unit must be at most 25% of the house's total floor area and at least 400 sq ft, so the house needs at least 1,600 sq ft of floor area, not counting garages, attics without floors, open porches, cellars or space under 6 ft high.

types_allowed.note: Inside the existing house, including an attached garage or upper story, with additions meeting the district's area and bulk rules, or 'Contained within a new or an existing accessory building on the same lot'

max_share_of_house.note: 'no more than 25% of the principal dwelling's total floor area'. Floor area leaves out garages, carports, attics without floors, open porches, terraces, cellars and space with a ceiling under 6 ft (350-201 'Floor area')

min_sqft.note: 'shall have a minimum floor area of 400 square feet'. A house needs at least 1,600 sq ft of floor area for 25% to reach 400 sq ft

owner_occupancy.note: 'Either the principal single-family dwelling or the supplemental dwelling unit shall be occupied by the bona fide owner of the property'

family_only.note: No family rule for the supplemental dwelling unit. The agricultural accessory dwelling unit is for family members or farm workers (350-1101B(9)(a))

max_adus.note: 'No more than one supplemental dwelling unit shall be allowed on each lot. If the lot is greater than 10 acres, two supplemental dwellings units are allowed.'

max_adus_by_lot_size.note: One on each lot, two on a lot greater than 10 acres

max_height_ft.note: Accessory uses in 350-1101C, including their buildings, have 'A maximum height of 15 feet, except as otherwise expressly permitted in this chapter'. Read for a unit in an accessory building. On a farm, agricultural accessory uses follow the district height (350-1101B), see the other paths

setback_side_ft.note: 'for accessory buildings larger than 200 square feet, a minimum setback of not less than 15 feet from lot lines'. A unit of at least 400 sq ft is in a building over 200 sq ft

setback_rear_ft.note: Same 15 ft rule for an accessory building over 200 sq ft

front_yard_barred.note: 'Located in the rear or side yard of the lot' and 'no further forward on the tract or lot than the front line of the principal building, except for garages'. A garage may sit forward of the house's front line, but still not in the front yard

spaces_required.note: 'Two off street parking spaces shall be provided for a supplemental dwelling unit in addition to the parking requirements for the principal use'

fraction_rounding.note: 'a fraction of 1/2 or more shall be rounded up, and a fraction of less than 1/2 rounded down'

min_lot_sqft.note: A lot subdivided from a parent tract of 10 acres or more: one acre minimum and two acres maximum, 100 ft wide. A lot subdivided from a tract under 10 acres needs four acres and 200 ft of width (350-402D(1)). A farm needs 10 acres (350-402A). A lot that predates the chapter and was never split from a parent tract is a nonconforming lot question (350-1504)

max_impervious_coverage.note: 'Maximum lot coverage: 20%'. Lot coverage is the share of the lot 'covered by any and all impervious materials'

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling: two acres, 150 ft wide at the building line and 115 ft at the street
Conventional development option: two acres, 100 ft wide at the building line and 75 ft at the street, 0.5 dwelling units per acre of net tract area. A cluster lot is 20,000 sq ft (350-602A)

min_lot_replaced_in_planned_development.note: A lot in a cluster residential development takes the cluster figures: 20,000 sq ft, 60 ft wide

min_lot_sqft.note: 'Minimum lot area shall be 20,000 square feet, and the maximum lot area shall be one acre', 75 ft wide

setback_front_ft.note: The average of the adjacent buildings' front setbacks, at least 10 ft and at most 30 ft from the street line. The averaged figure may be larger than 10 ft

max_impervious_coverage.note: 'Maximum lot coverage: 25% for residential uses'. Lot coverage counts all impervious materials. The district sets no separate building coverage

min_lot_sqft.note: Facility Option 1, community or public water and sewer: 10,000 sq ft, 75 ft wide at the building line, density 4 dwelling units per acre of net tract area

max_impervious_coverage.note: 'Maximum lot coverage', which counts all impervious materials

Facility Option 3: individual water supply with public or community sewer
Facility Option 4: individual water supply and on-lot sewage system
